title: Ukraine Destroys Two Tu-142 Aircraft + Iskander-M System at Taganrog Airfield — Day 1,556
detail: Overnight into May 30, 2026 — Day 1,556 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces (1st Separate Unmanned Systems Center) struck Russia's military airfield at Taganrog in Rostov Oblast, destroying two Tu-142 long-range maritime patrol/anti-submarine aircraft and an Iskander-M operational-tactical ballistic missile system. Major Robert 'Madyar' Brovdi confirmed the operation and released video footage. The Tu-142 is a Soviet-designed long-range turboprop used for maritime reconnaissance, anti-submarine warfare, and electronic intelligence gathering; Russia has no active production line for the Tu-142, making each loss operationally irreplaceable for Russian Naval Aviation's Black Sea and Azov Sea surveillance capability. The Iskander-M is Russia's primary short-range tactical ballistic missile system; destroying a launcher degrades Russia's capacity to fire precision strikes against Ukrainian cities and frontline positions. The Taganrog airfield was previously struck by Ukraine's Neptune missile in April 2026 (Atlant Aero drone factory). Simultaneously, Zelensky confirmed strikes on a shadow-fleet tanker in Taganrog port and on a marine oil terminal in occupied Crimea during the same overnight operation window.

media.caption: Ukraine's 1st Separate Unmanned Systems Center destroys two Tu-142 aircraft and an Iskander-M at Taganrog military airfield — May 30, 2026

title: Ukraine Strikes Armavir Oil Depot (Krasnodar) + Taganrog Port Shadow Tanker; Barracuda Drones Hit Kherson Positions — Day 1,556
detail: On May 30, 2026 — Day 1,556 — Ukrainian long-range drones struck an oil depot in Armavir, Krasnodar Krai (~500 km from Ukraine's border) setting it ablaze, while simultaneously striking a shadow-fleet tanker in Taganrog port in Rostov Oblast. President Zelensky confirmed the Armavir strike and a separate hit on a marine oil terminal in occupied Crimea as part of the same overnight operation. The Armavir strike is part of Ukraine's 2026 campaign targeting Russian oil storage and export infrastructure — following Novorossiysk (May 23), Volgograd Lukoil refinery (May 29), Vtorovo (May 24), Tuapse (April 16, 20), and Baltic terminals at Ust-Luga and Primorsk (March 2026). Ukraine's Naval Forces also released footage of the 40th Separate Marine Brigade using Barracuda maritime drones to destroy Russian positions and military shelters in the Kherson region — demonstrating Ukraine's expanding multi-domain maritime strike capability in the Dnipro River delta. The shadow-fleet tanker struck in Taganrog port was transporting Russian oil in circumvention of Western sanctions. Ukraine's energy infrastructure campaign against Russia has now struck facilities in Krasnodar Krai, Volgograd, Vladimir, Leningrad, Moscow, Ryazan, and Yaroslavl oblasts — a geographic sweep indicating significant improvement in long-range drone capability.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes Armavir oil depot in Krasnodar Krai and shadow tanker in Taganrog port as deep-strike campaign intensifies — May 30, 2026

title: Russia Launches 291 Combat Attacks, 277 Guided Bombs, 8,549 Kamikaze Drones — Russian Losses Reach ~1,362,500 — Day 1,556
detail: On May 30, 2026 — Day 1,556 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine's General Staff reported 291 total combat engagements: 1 missile strike (7 missiles), 91 airstrikes, 277 guided aerial bombs (KABs), 8,549 kamikaze drones deployed, and 2,807 total attacks on populated areas and troop positions including 53 MLRS attacks. The scale of 277 guided aerial bombs (KABs — glide bombs launched from aircraft at stand-off range) in a single day continues Russia's attritional campaign devastating Ukrainian fixed defenses. Key frontline assault axes on May 30: 8 attacks near Starytsia, Lyman, and Vovchansk (Kharkiv Oblast); 12 penetration attempts toward Lyman, Drobysheve, Shyikivka, Ozerne, and Hlushchenkove; continued intense pressure in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors. Ukrainian MoD reported approximately 1,430 additional Russian personnel eliminated during the May 30 window, bringing cumulative losses to approximately 1,362,500 personnel since February 24, 2022. Simultaneously, ISW and Deep State map confirmed that the village of Novoselivka in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast was liberated from Russian occupation — a positive development amid the sustained aerial assault. 18 settlements across Kharkiv Oblast were shelled on May 30, killing 2 and injuring 4.

media.caption: Russia launches 291 combat attacks and 277 guided aerial bombs on Day 1,556 — cumulative Russian losses reach ~1,362,500 — May 30, 2026

title: Russian Drone Destroys Shostka Railway Station; Locomotive Engineer Killed; 976 Attacks on Zaporizhzhia in 24 Hours — Day 1,556
detail: On May 30, 2026 — Day 1,556 — Russian drone strikes hit multiple Ukrainian civilian and economic targets. In Sumy Oblast, a Russian drone destroyed the railway station building in Shostka (40 km from the Russian border) and damaged surrounding railway infrastructure — continuing Russia's systematic campaign to sever Ukraine's logistics network supplying both frontlines and civilians. In Chernihiv Oblast, a separate drone struck a company site, killing a 58-year-old civilian man and igniting a fire in the car park that destroyed 7 lorries. In Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Russian forces conducted 976 separate attacks on 55 settlements within 24 hours, killing 2 and injuring 7. A Russian drone struck a working locomotive on the Zaporizhzhia regional railway network, killing the locomotive engineer — an intentional strike on civilian transport workers. In Kharkiv Oblast, 18 settlements were shelled across the day, resulting in 2 killed and 4 injured. The simultaneous strikes on transport infrastructure across Sumy, Chernihiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Kharkiv oblasts demonstrate Russia's strategy of dispersed attacks designed to overwhelm Ukrainian air defenses while systematically degrading the civilian economy supporting Ukraine's war effort.

media.caption: Russian drone destroys Shostka railway station; locomotive engineer killed; Zaporizhzhia hit with 976 attacks in 24 hours — May 30, 2026
